original_question: For a rational polygon P, the quadratic constants c_*(P) and c^*(P) are defined by inequalities c_*(P) l^2 <= f_P(l) <= c^*(P) l^2 for all sufficiently large l. Find efficient estimates for these quadratic constants.
target_in_paper: Section IV, Problem 12: "Find efficient estimates for quadratic constants," together with the immediately preceding definition of the quadratic bounds for f_P(ℓ).
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct open problem in the paper. It has the right setting (rational polygon P), the right counting function f_P(ℓ), the right quadratic-growth inequalities, and the right task: estimating the constants c_*(P) and c^*(P), rather than asking the stronger follow-up question about existence of a limiting constant.
missing_details: The paper’s notion of a rational polygon is: every angle between sides is a rational multiple of π.
In Section IV, polygons are not assumed convex or simply connected; the billiard-table framework there is broader than the default simple-convex interpretation.
f_P(ℓ) is the number of periodic bands of billiard trajectories of length at most ℓ, not the number of individual periodic trajectories.

The surrounding context explains why bands are counted: even-periodic trajectories come in parallel bands, while odd-periodic trajectories are isolated and, for rational polygons, only finitely many occur.
The quadratic constants satisfy 0 < c_*(P) ≤ c^*(P) < ∞.
“For all sufficiently large ℓ” should be spelled out as: there exists a threshold ℓ_0(P) such that the inequalities hold for all ℓ ≥ ℓ_0(P).
The parameter ℓ is a length variable; the problem is about quadratic growth in geometric length, not a separate coding-length or word-complexity parameter.
To stay paper-faithful, the question should remain limited to estimating c_*(P) and c^*(P), and should not be broadened to the stronger Problem 13 asking whether f_P(ℓ)/ℓ^2 has a limit.
refined_question: Let P be a rational polygonal billiard table, meaning that every angle between sides of P is a rational multiple of π, and let f_P(ℓ) denote the number of periodic bands of billiard trajectories in P of Euclidean length at most ℓ. By results of Masur and Boshernitzan, there exist constants 0 < c_*(P) ≤ c^*(P) < ∞ and a threshold ℓ_0(P) such that c_*(P)ℓ^2 ≤ f_P(ℓ) ≤ c^*(P)ℓ^2 for all ℓ ≥ ℓ_0(P). Obtain efficient estimates for the quadratic constants c_*(P) and c^*(P).
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper’s exact official open problem: Problem 12 in Section IV. The immediately preceding text there defines the counting function f_P(ℓ), states the quadratic inequalities for rational polygons, and names c_*(P), c^*(P) the quadratic constants; Problem 12 then asks for efficient estimates of those constants. The same page immediately continues with Problem 13, which asks a different and strictly stronger question about whether f_P(ℓ)/ℓ^2 converges, so the refined question should stop short of that. Section V.D later discusses periodic complexity and situates Problem 11 in a broader complexity framework, which helps confirm that the intended scope here is the periodic-orbit counting problem from Section IV, not a broader neighboring problem.
